title: Master equation for systems interacting with linearized gravity
authors: Oliviero Angeli, Anirudh Gundhi, Angelo Bassi
abstract: We investigate the open quantum dynamics of a system of two masses interacting with an environment of linearized gravitational waves. We formulate the analysis in terms of the observable proper distance between the two masses, and show that the canonical variables obtained from the standard Lagrangian, expressed in terms of the Fermi normal coordinates, are not suitable for an effective description of the system. We resolve this issue through a unitary transformation that provides a physically meaningful system--environment decomposition and derive the master equation to leading order in $G$. Its dissipative sector reproduces the classical energy loss due to gravitational-wave emission, while the noisy contributions suppress coherences between states with different mass quadrupole, or effectively, different proper separations. In the regime where the proper distance can be described by considering small quantum fluctuations around an average distance $l_0$, the dynamics reduces to a Caldeira--Leggett-type equation, with a decoherence rate dependent on the baseline length $l_0$.
summary: This paper develops a theoretical framework to describe how a mechanical system loses energy and decoheres when coupled to the environment of linearized gravitational waves. By deriving a master equation using specialized unitary transformations, the authors successfully reproduce known classical results for energy loss while predicting quantum decoherence effects.
main_problem: The paper investigates the open quantum dynamics of a system (two masses) interacting with an environment composed of linearized gravitational waves.
main_result: A master equation is derived whose dissipative sector correctly reproduces classical energy loss due to gravitational-wave emission, and the dynamics reduce to a Caldeira-Leggett type equation in the small fluctuation limit.
method: The authors employ unitary transformations to achieve a physically meaningful system-environment decomposition before deriving the master equation perturbatively in the weak field limit of linearized gravity.
